affectedPublicSurfaces: None. This slice edits backend/src/juli_backend/workers/tasks/agent_workflow.py and backend/src/juli_backend/services/agent/runner/{core,tool_executor}.py only. journeys.name: runner-celery-interface-reconciliation
assertions: run_agent_workflow constructs the real WorkflowRunner with its seven keyword arguments, not the removed _RunnerProtocol placeholder
resume_agent_workflow calls WorkflowRunner.resume(workflow_run_id, approved=...) matching the real signature
the _RunnerProtocol placeholder is deleted, as its own docstring instructed once W3-A landed
core.py threads block.call_id into ToolExecutor.execute as tool_call_id
a WRITE tool dispatched through WorkflowRunner reaches the ToolExecutionLedger claim-then-execute path, which was previously unreachable
a WRITE tool dispatched through WorkflowRunner reaches ConcurrencyGuard.check_before_write, which was previously never constructed
READ tools still skip the ledger entirely, per ADR-073 d.3
the existing reviewed suites for #1119, #1120, #1121, #1122 and #1123 pass unchanged

htmlRoutes: No HTML route or asset changes in this slice.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration. #1117 already shipped every column involved, including the tool_executions ledger key. This slice only changes which arguments are passed at existing call sites.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. The ledger and concurrency guard remain implemented but structurally inert, which is the state Wave 3 is in today — safe, because a write that cannot reach the ledger simply takes the ordinary path, and no idempotency claim is being relied on in production.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. That returns the ledger and guard to inert, restoring exactly the pre-merge behaviour. The revert is confined to argument passing at three call sites plus the task shells; no schema or data is affected, so nothing needs repair.

notes: Wiring slice unblocking #1124 and #1133. Wave 3 decomposed into 17 slices and none owned reconciling the Celery task shells with the real WorkflowRunner, or threading tool_call_id so the ledger and guard become reachable. Recorded as a Meta decomposition gap in #1145.
doNotInfer: Do not infer that this slice makes the live gates pass. #1124's two smokes do not exist, #1133's observed browser run has not happened, and AGENT_WORKFLOWS_ENABLED is wired into no systemd unit and no api.env.example -- a real deployment still cannot exercise any of this even though the enqueue and cancel-signal mechanics now exist.

Do not infer that a run started via POST /v1/demo/runs actually completes end to end. The enqueue path is real -- the route creates the workflow_runs row and calls run_agent_workflow.delay(str(run_id)) -- but _construct_runner's three composition seams (_default_llm_service, _default_tool_registry, _default_playbook) still raise RunnerCompositionUnavailableError under workers/'s real import boundary, so a live worker still cannot construct an LLM service, tool registry or playbook. This gap is pre-existing, not introduced or closed by this change.

Do not infer that cancel has been observed against a real running loop. workflow_runs.cancel_requested is genuinely written by POST /v1/demo/runs/{id}/cancel and read fresh (never a cached snapshot) by _construct_runner's cancel_check on every WorkflowRunner checkpoint poll -- proven by tests, including a mutation-tested proof that a Session.get()-based (cached) implementation is wrong. But no live run has ever actually been cancelled mid-execution: #1133's browser-observed run has not happened, and the composition-seam gap above means a live run cannot even start yet.
Do not infer that idempotency has been exercised against a real vendor. Reachability is proven by tests; the verify-then-decide branch has still never met a real TikTok response.
